title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Once the Bearer of the Curse has finally cleared the way to the Throne and acquired the means to access it, Nashandra will intercept them and reveal her true form. She then declares the Bearer of the Curse worthy to assume her intended role for Vendrick, to have their power usurped by her so she can claim the throne for herself.

The Bearer of the Curse has grown too strong however, and Nashandra falls at their hand.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
Throne of Want -  Dark Souls II - location - plot 
 plot : The Throne of Want is the final location in *Dark Souls II*, where the Bearer of the Curse must best the Throne Watcher and Defender and Nashandra to become a true monarch and claim the Throne. However, if the player has killed Vendrick before Nashandra, Aldia will appear as the final boss.

The Emerald Herald also makes an appearance at the Throne’s entrance where she reveals her true name. In the aftermath, either she or Aldia will narrate the game’s ending.

The area can only be accessed through use of the King's Ring. And the throne itself and only be reached with the Giant's Kinship.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
At a certain moment during his reign, Nashandra came to Drangleic, she coveted the Throne of Want and the power of the First Flame, and seduced Vendrick in order to use him as a means to accomplish her goal, becoming his queen.

Much time later, after Drangleic was ravaged due to both the war with the Giants and the undead curse, which all of Vendrick’s and Aldia’s plans to cure were in vain, Vendrick found out about Nashandra's plan: to use the throne to claim the First Flame for herself. Vendrick reacted quickly and sent the Throne Watcher and the Throne Defender to guard the throne. He then fled to the Undead Crypt, where he eventually went Hollow, to keep his ring and soul from the wrong hands. He did all this in an attempt to stop Nashandra.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : **Nashandra** or **Queen Nashandra** is a boss and the main antagonist of *Dark Souls II*. She is fought at the end of the Throne of Want area, only after the player has obtained the Giant's Kinship; if the Throne Watcher and Defender have not already been defeated, Nashandra's boss fight will trigger automatically after theirs.

Although she is the final boss of the base game, the *Scholar of the First Sin* expansion added Aldia as a potential "true" final boss, whose battle triggers after Nashandra's if conditions are met. Prior to her boss fight, she appears as a special character in human form atop Drangleic Castle, where she can be talked to from afar.

title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
Throne of Want -  Dark Souls II - location - description 
 description : The true throne of Drangleic, hidden away deep beneath Drangleic Castle in a great cavern accessible only to those with the symbol of the King. A long, jagged pathway extending down from the final gate in the depths of the castle leads to a kiln guarded by the last of Vendrick's guardians, the Throne Watcher and Defender. These warriors serve as the last bulwark against Nashandra claming the throne, and by extension, gaining the power of the First Flame.

The actual throne takes the form of a great stone slab carved into the form of a throne, surrounded by a kiln of ash-covered stone, across a gap filled with Golems that aid the true monarch to their rightful place

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
Throne of Want -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : The Throne of Want serves as a means to link the First Flame, in a way similar to the thrones of Lothrics’s Firelink Shrine, as it is built inside a kiln and the ashes that cover it seems to indicate the remains of previous Lords of Cinder.

While it’s exact origins are unknown, the structure and ashes surrounding the Throne imply that it is much more ancient than the Kingdom of Drangleic.

According to Vendrick and Nashandra, once Vendrick sougth the fire, for he believed that by linking it he could end the Undead Curse. But he would later discover that this was a lie, since the flame would fade again and the curse return every time, he then refused to sit on the Throne and decided to search for a permanent way to end the curse.

title: Drangleic
snippet: In the darkest hour of his reign, Vendrick also realized that his Queen, Nashandra, was a creature of the Abyss, and harbored an insatiable desire for strength. She was a fragment of a dark creature taken a human form, obsessed with the King's powerful soul. Impelled by her cravings, Nashandra sought souls, and strove to make the strength of the Giants her own, everything to reach the Throne of Want and the link for the First Flame so it could spread the Dark. Her painting in the castle was in fact able to curse the undead, making them hollow and draining their life, and only the king knew whether the depiction of the Queen was a resentful mockery, or an affectionate exaltation. At this point Vendrick had achieved a profound understanding of the truths of the world. He understood how the fire of souls was not enough to harness the curse, and how the Flame would soon fade and the souls of ancient beings would reemerge, before Dark would descend as a curse on humans, making them take

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Shanalotte will once again appear once the Bearer of the Curse has reached the Dragon Aerie. Here, she will reveal that it was her manifestations that led them here, and has been guiding them all along. She directs the Bearer to the top of the aerie, where the Ancient Dragon awaits them.

Shanalotte will appear one final time when the Bearer of the Curse is approaching the Throne of Want. She will tell the Bearer of her origins and her true name. She will warn them that Nashandra, desiring the power of the Flame and the Great Soul will come after them, but that they must persist nonetheless.

Should the Bearer of the Curse choose to claim the throne, Shanalotte will narrate their ascent, explaining that linking the flame will cause souls to flourish anew but that the events that have transpired will play out all over again, and that it is the Bearer's choice whether to embrace or renounce this.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse fights their way through the knights and defeats Velstadt, finding Vendrick at last. The King, however, has been reduced to a hollow, wandering the grounds aimlessly. The Bearer may choose to put the king out of his misery, or leave him to wander endlessly. Here, the Bearer of the Curse finds the King's Ring, and the Emerald Herald, who tells them that the ring will open the way to the far east, where the Bearer of the Curse must journey next. She proceeds to warn the Bearer that if they continue on this path, they too will one day walk these grounds without really remembering why.

Should the Bearer of the Curse seek her council, Nashandra too will direct the Bearer of the Curse to follow the symbol of the King.

snippet: Vendrick fled the Castle through the King's Passage never to return, fearing Nashandra's wickedness. He left the Looking Glass Knight behind him, ready to expunge those who would challenge him, forever true to his original command, as the first line of defense against those who would attempt to pursue the runaway king into the Undead Crypt. The king took with him only a handful of Royal Soldiers and the faithful Sir Velstadt, and found refuge in the Shrine of Amana. Vendrick was initially intent on reaching the Throne of Want and link the First Flame but in the end the king understood that if he did so, Nashandra would have gained an easy access to the throne connected to the Flame. Vendrick thus decided to free himself from his soul, abandoning it among the ruins, to descend even deeper into the Undead Crypt. Here, left alone, he isolated himself in a secluded room wearing only his robes, crown, sword and his ring. Overcome by nihilism, Vendrick was consumed by the curse and soon

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Any summoned characters or players who survived the fight between the Throne Watcher and Defender will stay with the host to defeat Nashandra; however, they will not receive two rewards (Token of Fidelity or Sunlight Medal).
By burning a Bonfire Ascetic on the King's Gate bonfire in Drangleic Castle, Nashandra can be respawned.
Wearing the Black Witch Veil, Hollow Skin, or any of the four crowns already infused with Vendrick's blessing will grant immunity to Curse; however, the player will still take continual damage whenever near the curse fountains.

If a Bonfire Ascetic is used, then once the Watcher and Defender are both defeated and their souls received, Nashandra's boss fight will ensue immediately.
Both bosses can be parried.
The Throne Defender Set and Throne Watcher Set will be sold by Maughlin the Armorer in Majula after defeating them.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Once arriving at the Dragon Shrine bonfire, the Scholar appears once more. He will reveal that he is in fact Aldia, the elder brother of Vendrick. Aldia says that he "sought to shed the yoke of fate, but failed" and that he now only awaits an answer. He asks of the Bearer of the Curse to "seek the Throne, seek light, dark and what lies beyond", for the last time, he'll vanish into the flames, allowing the Bearer of the Curse to light the bonfire.

The Ancient Dragon will give the Bearer the Ashen Mist Heart, which allows one to peer into the memories of things long withered. Should the Bearer of the Curse again seek out Nashandra's council, she will warn that the dragon is a false deity and is in fact no more than a prop. Still, she will direct the Bearer of the Curse to go to the Forest of Fallen Giants, to use the Ashen Mist Heart to peer into the Giants' memories.

The woman warned the king of a country of Giants beyond the Northern Sea, creatures that possessed souls of immense power and that apparently presented an impending threat to his kingdom. title: Drangleic
snippet: Thanks to this discovery Vendrick became the monarch who came closest to becoming a true "King" and turning his wants into reality. He had access to the primordial Flame whose power could decide the fate of the world, either by linking it to prolong the state of the world or refusing this fate and leading the world to darkness as a Dark Lord. Vendrick, however, never made either decision and continued to reign over Drangleic. Both he and his brother were not convinced by the two possible choices and, anchored to the illusion of the form that life had during the Age of Fire, they looked for a way to maintain it, searching for a way to free humans from the curse of Undeath and breaking the seal of fire that imprisoned them. As he deepened his knowledge of souls and curses, Vendrick effectively reigned over Drangleic, protecting the country from any external threats. Nashandra helped bring peace to the kingdom, a peace so profound that it reminded humans of the Dark from which they came.

title: Firelink Shrine (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The opening area is a large circular chamber where five great thrones face a central bonfire, the only bonfire guarded by a Firekeeper in the whole game. Each of the five thrones looks different and unique, fitting the Lord of Cinder it is made for: The first draped with a extravagant red cloth and covered in saintly candles; the next plain and lightly decorated; the center is heavily charred with molten streaks and half-melted features; the next is flanked with a number of swords besides it; and the final is much too large for any normal human to sit upon. All of these thrones (save the second) are missing their respective Lords, and thus the Unkindled must find them and force their cinders to be seated.

Below the main entrance is a tunnel that leads to a back chamber. The Shrine Handmaid sells goods here, and Blacksmith Andre smiths goods here. Throughout the journey, the Unkindled can recruit a number of vendors and tutors to get new gear and learn new spells.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Studying and experimenting on the inhuman creatures and their souls, and via studies on artifacts from older kingdoms, Vendrick and Aldia pioneered the creation of Golems, very similar in appearance to the captured giants. Vendrick made Nashandra his queen, and had the golems build his Royal Castle, as proof of his gratitude and affection to her. Beneath the royal castle was the ancient Throne of Want, an artifact capable of connecting to the First Flame, the source of souls and beginning of all that the king was seeking. Studying the First Flame and the mysteries of the soul with his brother Aldia, the king acquired a profound understanding of the history of the world and the rules of reality, how the Flame brought Disparity and everything from it, propagating souls in the world every time someone linked it, giving it new strength. He also understood how the Dark was kept under control as long as the fire flourished, and that once the fire naturally weakened the curse would strike

title: Giant's Kinship
snippet:
Giant's Kinship -  Dark Souls II - shield - trivia 
 trivia : Japanese translations reveal that the item's name is a mistranslation and that properly translates to "The Resonance With The Giants". It is not a physical item, but something the Bearer of the Curse gains from combating the Giants and the Giant Lord.
The original Japanese item description reads: "There is a throne fitting for each king. The view from the throne is known only to the one who sits upon it. Or does the throne show he who sits upon it what they want to see?".

title: Ending (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - leave_the_throne 
 leave_the_throne : Available only to those with the *Scholar of the First Sin* version or any patch newer than 1.10 for the original *Dark Souls II*.

This ending only becomes available after the player has defeated Vendrick in the Undead Crypt and after having spoken to Aldia at every bonfire he spawns at throughout the game. Upon defeating Nashandra, Aldia will fight the player as an additional final boss. Upon defeating Aldia, both endings are available to the player, and choosing to exit the Throne of Want through the fog wall will result in this ending.

In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse rejects the throne, and bitterly walks away, seemingly to seek another, more permanent way to end the curse.

title: Golem
snippet:
Golem -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lore 
 lore : The giant stone Golems are a creation of King Vendrick who used the object he stole from the Giants to create them. They are also the builders of Drangleic Castle, and throughout the castle they are used in a variety of ways such as torch sconces as well as door openers when powered with souls. In the Throne of Want, there are noticeably taller Golems that surround the Throne and upon Nashandra's death they animate and form a bridge to the throne.

title: Ending (Dark Souls II)
snippet:

 proceed_to_throne : After the player defeats Nashandra (or Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin, if his conditions are met) at the Throne of Want, a cutscene will play showing the player walking atop the golems, who create a bridge for the player to cross, and into a throne room. In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse will accept their part in the cycle of the world and take the throne. Doing so means that they will either sacrifice themselves to link the flame, or allow the flame to continue to fade and become the Dark Lord. Which the Bearer of the Curse chooses is known only to them.

title: Throne Watcher and Defender
snippet:
Throne Watcher and Defender -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Throne Watcher** and the **Throne Defender** are dual bosses in *Dark Souls II*. They are fought at the end of the Throne of Want area, which can be accessed with the King's Ring.

They are both fought at once with individual health bars; when one is slain, their health is restored shortly after by the other, meaning that their respective health points must be reduced to zero in quick succession. If the player possesses the Giant's Kinship, Nashandra's boss fight will trigger immediately after the Watcher and Defender's.

snippet:

 description : Each king has his rightful throne. And when he sits upon it, he sees what he chooses to see.

Or perhaps, it is the throne, which shows the king only what he wants.

The flames roar, but will soon begin to fade, and only a worthy heir might burnish their light. What is it, truly, a claimant of the throne could desire?

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - epilogue 
 epilogue : ***Proceed to the Throne:** In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse will accept their part in the cycle of the world, and take the throne. Doing so means that they will either sacrifice themselves to link the flame, or allow the flame to continue fading and become the Dark Lord. Which the Bearer of the Curse chooses is unknown.

***Leave the Throne: **In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse rejects the throne, and bitterly walks away, seemingly to seek another, more permanent way to end the curse.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : Aldia during his boss fight can be in either "flame" mode or “burnt out" mode.
**In "flame" mode, he has very high damage reduction and creates an aura, which may seriously wound the player.
If the player killed Nashandra before downloading the patch, Aldia will not appear in the Throne of Want, even if he has been spoken to in all three previous locations. A Bonfire Ascetic must be burned at the King's Gate bonfire to spawn Aldia, which means the player must defeat Nashandra as well as the Throne Watcher and Defender again before being able to fight Aldia.
During the fight, spears and shields with high fire resistance are recommended.
Aldia drops nothing upon defeat, not even souls. The only reward from defeating him is that the player has the option to leave the throne, giving the player an alternate ending.

title: Giant's Kinship
snippet:
Giant's Kinship -  Dark Souls II - shield - usage

title: Scythe of Want

Scythe of Want -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : A scythe born from the soul of Nashandra.

The old one of the Abyss was reborn in death, split into miniscule fragments, and spread across the land. The pieces began to coalesce once again, becoming human in shape.

title: Golem
snippet:
Golem -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : Aldia serves as a lore-centric character, alluding to a great deal of things in relation to the lore of *Dark Souls II*.

When the Bearer of the Curse has defeated the Four Great Ones and lit the Primal Bonfires he will emerge and guide the Bearer of the Curse towards his brother Vendrick, now a mindless hollow. He continues to appear to the Bearer of the Curse, seeking to learn their intentions and telling them of the nature of the curse and the fabric of their world.

He will finally attack the Bearer of the Curse before they can take the Throne of Want, seeking to test them. When Aldia is defeated, he will ask what the Bearer of the Curse wants: light, dark or something else entirely. If the Bearer of the Curse chooses to reject the throne and leave, Aldia will narrate the Bearer of the Curse's departure from the throne.

title: Chime of Want
snippet:
Chime of Want -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Sacred chime created from the soul of Nashandra. Greatly amplifies spells.

The old one of the Abyss was reborn in death, split into miniscule fragments, and spread across the land.
The tiniest of these pieces, precisely due to its size, was the first to restore its form.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - locations 
 locations : #He is first encountered in the final primal bonfire room that remains unlit. If all bonfires have been lit prior to downloading the patch, he will automatically appear in the Black Gulch primal bonfire room, after The Rotten.
#Upon speaking to the player at the primal bonfire, Aldia will proceed to the first bonfire in the Undead Crypt.
#After exhausting his dialogue in the Undead Crypt, Aldia can be found in the Dragon Shrine bonfire room, at a significantly reduced size compared to the first bonfire.
#Finally, after completing the dialogue in Dragon Shrine, Aldia will appear as a boss in the Throne of Want in Drangleic Castle after killing Nashandra, but only if Vendrick is killed before Nashandra. The game can be completed without fighting Aldia here, if Nashandra is killed before Vendrick is.

title: Salaman the Master Pyromancer
snippet:
Salaman the Master Pyromancer -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Salaman's name is still shared by the Pyromancers of the Great Swamp, as well as the legends of his prodigious tutelage. Many pyromancers seek the tomes from which he learned the art, believing him to have known the primal chaos pyromancies. It is unclear what would have prompted Quelana to teach him these, as she does not teach any chaos pyromancy to the Chosen Undead.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet: **The nature of the Pilgrims of Londor, and what the death they seek means to them, are left unexplained, but it is worth noting that if the player makes Yuria hostile, she claims that "Yoel knows not of thy folly," speaking of him in the present tense even though he will always have died by the time she appears.

title: Dark Set
snippet:
Dark Set -  Dark Souls - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Dark Set offers a unique blend of good protection, decent Poise and low weight; it is one of the lighter medium sets. What sets it apart is that, though its defense is wholly unspectacular compared to some of the other high-level medium sets, it stands above many of them in terms of defense for each unit of weight. As such, it is especially valuable for players who want good poise and defense, but want to minimize the weight involved with such a choice.

Light and Dark are two sides of the same coin, much like the soul and the curse. The beings who presented themselves to those in search of kinghood were drawn to their awesome strength.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_ancients 
 age_of_ancients : Long ago, the world was an unformed, homogeneous place which lacked a true concept of disparity. The grey, rocky land was perpetually shrouded in fog, and the landscape was dominated by towering stone archtrees which extended into endless clouds. The everlasting dragons, ancient and immortal entities who transcended the later concepts of life and death, were the dominant beings. This period was known as the Age of Ancients.

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - lead 
 lead : **The First Flame** is a storyline concept in the *Dark Souls *series.

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_fire 
 age_of_fire : With the dragons defeated, the Lords took over the world, ruling as Gods from their seat of power in the land of Lordran. It was a prosperous era, and many nations were born. In time, however, the First Flame began to fade, and with it the power of the Gods, leading to an era of decay and the emergence of the Undead Curse. If the Flame were to gutter out completely, it would end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Kiln of the First Flame
snippet:
Kiln of the First Flame -  Dark Souls - location - description 
 description : This area is accessed by offering to the Lordvessel the souls of Bed of Chaos, the Four Kings, Gravelord Nito, and Seath the Scaleless in the Firelink Altar.
